title: [RTPS] Fix PSK dissection of AES256 encoded messages
description:
The attached captures were previously failing because:

* Receiver specific MACs are optional.
* AAD is compulsary.
* Messages may have Header Extension submessages.

[wireshark_aes256.zip](/uploads/b016ca6a9c7a6b9f94cd0adf5d8343a7/wireshark_aes256.zip)

This PR solves the problems, allowing dissection of PSK-encoded messages.

`tvb_memdup(pinfo->pool, ...)` (pinfo->pool since it's stored in a pinfo->pool allocated object) would be simpler than calling `g_memdup2`.
It would also have the advantage that you wouldn't have to manually free it.

Do you *really* want to memset a length of `RTPS_HE_MESSAGE_LENGTH_FLAG` (i.e., 2), and not the full length of 4 octets that the field takes up. Are you confusing the value of the flag with the actual length of the optional field that the flag refers to?
`header_extension_length` is *unsigned* not signed. Yes, it *should not* be so large as that would matter, but we have to worry about fuzzed data.

It doesn't matter if you store a 16-bit unsigned quantity in a signed integer, that's not a problem, but if you use `tvb_get_int16` to retrieve it from the frame, it will sign extend it and make it negative in cases it's not supposed to be.
Here you trust `header_extension_length` when deciding how much memory to duplicate.

Here you trust `offsetToHeaderExtensionData`, which comes from the *flags* in the packet, when deciding the offset to memset. What if the octetsToNextHeader is *inconsistent* with the flags? Then you have memory corruption.
